newsitem.title: CHINA: THAI BAILOUT IN HK'S LONG TERM INTEREST-HK'S TUNG.
newsitem.headline: THAI BAILOUT IN HK'S LONG TERM INTEREST-HK'S TUNG.

text.p: Hong Kong's leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Tuesday the rescue package to bail out Thailand was in Hong Kong's long-term interest and he is confident that Bangkok would be able to repay the money.
"This is an important issue. It is something that ought to be done. It is a worthy thing to do," Tung told reporters.
"It is in the consideration of Hong Kong's long-term interest," he said.
Hong Kong will contribute US$1 billion to a US$16 billion bailout package for Thailand.
The package was organised by the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which called a meeting of bankers in Tokyo, including the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA).
Thailand was the first victim of a wave of speculative selling that spread to other currencies in the region, including Malaysia, Indonesia, the Philippines and Singapore.

"The IMF will require Thailand to follow certain conditions in running its economy and financial markets in the future. There shouldn't be any problem," Tung said in a response to question whether Thailand would be able to repay the loans to Hong Kong and other countries.
The package includes contributions from Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Korea, Japan and the IMF.
